# `m.futures.schedules`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Futures schedules: the timed events of each product's trading sessions.

```python
m.futures.schedules(*, product_code=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `session_end_date.gte` and `session_end_date.lte` |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `ProductCode`, `TradingVenue`, `Timestamp` and `Event` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `trading_venue`, `trading_venue_any_of`, `trading_venue_gt`, `trading_venue_gte`, `trading_venue_lt`, `trading_venue_lte` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `product_code` | Only this product (`"ES"`) or these (`["ES", "NQ"]`); None for every product. A table of codes, in a `ProductCode` column, reads each code as if passed alone; a refreshing one is followed by `fetch()` and re-read by each `poll()` cycle. |  |
| `start` | The first session, by `SessionEndDate`, inclusive; a calendar date. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last session, inclusive; None also returns future sessions. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | The endpoint sorts by `product_code`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | Needs `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Such as `{"trading_venue": "XCME"}`; never `session_end_date`, which `start` and `end` set. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Schedules (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Futures Basic | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Starter | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Developer | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Advanced | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CME | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CBOT | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business NYMEX | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business COMEX | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `timestamp`: "The timestamp for the given market event." | REST |
| `Event` | String | The type of session on the given trading date. | REST |
| `ProductCode` | String | The product code of the futures contract. | REST |
| `ProductName` | String | The name of the futures product to which this schedule applies. | REST |
| `SessionEndDate` | String | The session end date (also known as the trading date) of the session the event belongs to. Trading sessions end at 5 PM Central Time, so a session ending at 5 PM CT on January 1st has a session_end_date of 2025-01-01. | REST |
| `TradingVenue` | String | The trading venue (MIC) for the exchange on which this schedule's product trades. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
